_comment: Bigness at its limit, wherever bigness is a thing the part of the world can be -- `size` is one name
on the sun, the curtain, the bow and a feature, so one word says it about all of them and attachment
decides which is meant: `colossal landmass` is the rock, `colossal sun` the star, `colossal trees
features` the wood, and a colossal Age is every one of them.
**The top of the axis, with `enormous` the step below it** (Jonah, 2026-08-31). Two words for big are
worth having only where they do different things, so this is 1.0 and that is 0.7 upward. `sweeping`
was the aurora's own word for the same 1.0 and went into this one when the names were shared.
The query is flat rather than keyed because `monumental` means the same thing everywhere it is
carried; a sun carries no tags at all, so asking it costs nothing and finds nothing.
